Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

mind verb

object, be bothered

also do you mind?, I don’t mind, if you don’t mind, would you mind

classical

Catull. 55.1: sī forte nōn molestum est
Cic. Clu. 168: tū autem, nisi molestum est, paulisper exsurge
Traupman 103: sī tibi molestum nōn est

molestum est

it bothers (someone); do you mind?

With a dative of the person. Nisi molestum est or sī nōn molestum est: if you don’t mind.

Other words

  • molestē ferre — mind, take it badly

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.22.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 103: istuc quidem nōn molestē ferō

    Nōn molestē ferō: I don’t mind.

  • nōn moror — I don’t mind, I have no objection

    also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 459: Ubi vīs, nōn moror.; Ant. in Cic. Phil. 13.35: nihil moror eōs salvōs esse

    Lewis & Short: “I have no objection”.

Examples

  • ōrāmus, sī forte nōn molestum est, dēmōnstrēs ubi sint tuae tenebrae

    Please, if you don’t mind, show us where your hiding place is.Catull. 55.1–2

  • Ubi vīs, nōn moror.

    Whenever you like; I’ve no objection.Ter. Eun. 459

See also never mind, it makes no difference, care, mind your fingers.
